> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee75aae1a8ebc2625e57074527d446151535634b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0969ed145600f546d4d07c37b1993a4ee833f3c9 && git checkout 0969ed145600f546d4d07c37b1993a4ee833f3c9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ee75aae1a8ebc2625e57074527d446151535634b ee5b089bbe2533d9d3044b93f4b64d6d57b5bb3a && git checkout -B drift-repro ee75aae1a8ebc2625e57074527d446151535634b && git merge --no-ff ee5b089bbe2533d9d3044b93f4b64d6d57b5bb3a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee75aae1a8ebc2625e57074527d446151535634b
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ee75aae1a8ebc2625e57074527d446151535634b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ee5b089bbe2533d9d3044b93f4b64d6d57b5bb3a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20827 (body and all 11 comments, the ruling `5910124148`, step one `5917187437`, the dispatch claim `5947645436`, the dev report `5950037486`), PR #21390 (body, 16-file list, net diff against `main`, its one comment), the check-runs on the head, and files at the head sha through `git show` only. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`FieldSchema` narrows** — a `select` / `radio` whose `options` is absent or `[]` and whose `picklist` is absent is refused at parse with a `custom` issue on the `options` path. RIGHT: ruling A orders exactly this on the `0fb8760bec` precedent, and the door sits beside the `reference` check in the same superRefine. The predicate is read, not restated: `checkFieldCompleteness` filtered to `FIELD_CHOICE_WITHOUT_OPTIONS` at `error`. At this head that module has `DEAD_WITHOUT_OPTIONS_ERROR = {select, radio}`, `hasOptionSource = hasEntries(options) || typeof picklist === 'string'`, `hasEntries` = non-empty array, and zero `import` statements, so the new data-to-kernel edge closes no cycle and no export is added (the dev's claim holds). The three consequences the shared predicate fixes — `options: []` is the same hole, `picklist` is a source, `checkboxes` (warning) and `multiselect` / `tags` (non-rule) keep parsing — are each pinned per type in `field.test.ts`, plus a document-level pin at `fields.status.options`.
2. **Reach of the narrowing** — every schema embedding `FieldSchema` at this head: `ObjectSchema.fields`, `ObjectExtensionSchema.fields`, the standalone `field` metadata type (`metadata-type-schemas.ts`), `system/migration.zod.ts` `addField.field`, `ui/widget.zod.ts` `field`. All RIGHT. The one that could have refused a legitimate shape is `ObjectExtensionSchema` (an override of an existing `select` relying on the base's options), but `objectql/src/registry.ts` `mergeObjectDefinitions` merges `fields` by per-key replacement (`{ ...base.fields, ...extension.fields }`), so an optionless `select` override was already a dead field at runtime; refusing it at parse is the ADR-0049 move. The only in-tree extension with a `select` (showcase `account.extension.ts`) carries options.
3. **Served picklist shape** — `PicklistServedFieldSchema` is a separate `looseObject` with `options.min(1)`, and `PicklistSchema.options` is `.min(1)`, so a picklist-bound field is never re-parsed into the hole. RIGHT, no served-shape regression.
4. **Stored rows** — not rewritten; `getMetaItem` serves with `_diagnostics.valid: false` at `fields.status.options`; `loadMetaFromDb` counts `invalid: 1` and still registers; `migrateStoredMetadata({ apply: true })` on a legacy row reports `failed`, writes no history row, leaves the bytes. RIGHT: this is the ruling's "some rows exist" arm (read and named, since no migration can invent options), and all three are new pins in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`.
5. **Public type surface widens** — `NumberComparandDoorFixtureField` and `TextOperatorDoorFixtureField` (both reach the public entry through `export *` in `data/index.ts`) gain an optional readonly `options` member. RIGHT, additive; `check:api-surface` records that an export exists, not its shape, so its "unchanged" is the expected reading, not a miss.
6. **Describe texts** on `options` / `picklist` changed, so `content/docs/references/data/field.mdx`, `data/object.mdx`, `system/migration.mdx` regenerated. RIGHT: `Type Check · source gates`, the job that runs `check:docs`, is `success` on this head.
7. **Hand-written docs** — `troubleshooting.mdx` heading renamed from a message no code emits ("Required property missing: options") to the real refusal; no inbound link to the old anchor exists at this head (grep over content, skills, packages). `validation-rules.mdx` now grades `multiselect` optional and `checkboxes` warning, matching the predicate. `field-types.mdx` `select` row rewritten; its `radio` / `multiselect` / `checkboxes` sections say "Same `options` property as `select`", and the refusal clause in that row names `select` and `radio` explicitly, so the multi types are not over-claimed. RIGHT. `formulas.mdx` example gained options. No `content/docs/releases/` or `CHANGELOG.md` touched.
8. **`Field.select([])`** emits `options: []` and now reaches the refusal. RIGHT: stated in the changeset and pinned; it is the ruling's "every door" reading, and `Field.select({ picklist })` and `Field.select(['Open', 'Closed'])` still pass (pinned).
9. **Fixture census** — 4 oversight fixtures plus the intended pin at `picklist.test.ts:129` (flipped into a refusal pin, its `checkFieldCompleteness` assertions kept) in spec; one `legacyObjectRow` row in two `metadata-protocol` files; `canonicalObjectRow` beyond the census for doc consistency. Matches step one exactly. RIGHT. Every helper the rewritten tests rely on (`issuesByPath`, `Field`, `ObjectSchema`, `SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES`) is already imported at this head.
10. **ADR-0078 relationship** — the ruling says "one more gate, not a replacement": the author-time rule and the `registry.ts` warn-never-throw twin are untouched (file list), and the registration seam still registers a stored optionless row (pinned). RIGHT against the ruling; see ③ for the ADR's own text.
11. **ADR anchors** — the one anchor on `field.zod.ts` (ADR-0120, `UniqueScopeSchema`) is symbol-based and the `system-context.mdx` census row anchors `field.zod.ts#readonly` by symbol, so the inserted lines move nothing. RIGHT.

Governed surfaces: none in the file list (`.changeset/`, `content/docs/`, `packages/`), and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`. This record is the dispatch's owed at-tier review, not a Tier S landing record. Size 344 changed lines over 16 files, well under the 5,000 human-merge threshold.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/20827-choice-door-select-radio-needs-options.md`: `"@objectstack/spec": minor`, summary `fix(spec)!:` with the bang, a `**BREAKING**` header, the migration in prose (FROM a `select` / `radio` with neither key TO `options: [{ label, value }]` or `picklist: 'NAME'`, or a `text` field when any value is meant to be allowed), the unchanged types named, and the stored-row prescription naming `GET /api/v1/meta/diagnostics` and the boot log's `field/choice-without-options` lines while saying the `os migrate meta --stored` preview does not find them. RIGHT: it is the `0fb8760bec` changeset's shape (`minor` plus BREAKING, same marker category), and `@objectstack/spec` is the only package that publishes a change — the `metadata-protocol` edits are tests only, `content/docs` does not publish. `skip-changeset` does not apply.
- **ADR-0087 marker**: one HTML-comment marker reading `not-required (no-migration-prescription) …`; the category is in `CATEGORIES` of `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, and the "why" closes the other four categories on facts (publishes, no id covers the rule, a schema narrowing not a runtime-interface-only or type-surface-only change). RIGHT. The gate verdicts: `Check Changeset` (pr-automation.yml, which runs `check-empty-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` against the merge base) is `success` on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes`** (PR body, changeset, and the dispatch claim `5947645436`). Valid: `yes` takes at least `minor` and the diff grades `minor`; the arm is optional by rule (`clause2-line.mjs`: "The arm is OPTIONAL, and that is a measurement"). The dev's own flag is right that `yes (narrowing)` is the fuller spelling — `clause2-line.mjs` defines it as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another", which is this diff (two fixture interfaces widen, `FieldSchema` narrows), and the step-one claim `5916083155` spelled it so. The breaking signal the arm exists to carry is already carried where the gate reads it (`**BREAKING**` plus bang, `[BREAKING+bang]`), so the bare `yes` loses nothing at any gate. Judged right as written; the owning seat may amend the PR-body line to `yes (narrowing)` before landing. Optional, not a condition.
- Cosmetic: PR title `feat(spec)!:` while the changeset says `fix(spec)!:` (the precedent used `fix`). No gate reads the pair together. Not a condition.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []` in the dev report — nothing to answer. The eight deviations and three out-of-scope findings, each answered or escalated:

1. **Clause-② spelling** — ANSWERED above: right as written, fuller spelling optional.
2. **`skills/objectstack-upgrade/references/examples-upgrade.md:105`** (`status: { type: 'select', required: true, storage: { notNull: true } }` inside `ObjectSchema.create`, in an `os:check` block whose intro says it "cannot rot into teaching a shape that no longer compiles") — VERIFIED at this head: the block is there, and `check-skill-examples.ts` type-checks with `tsc --noEmit` only, no `safeParse`, so no gate sees the parse refusal. ESCALATED: `skills/**` is Tier H and PD #14 says to split the governed file off, which the dev did. The fix is one `options` entry, valid before and after the door, so there is no ordering dependency; the owning seat should file the skills-lane PR now so the published skill does not teach a refused shape across a release. Not a condition on this PR.
3. **Blueprint** (`solution-blueprint.zod.ts:88` `options` optional; `:320` `.nullable()`) — VERIFIED at this head, and the module header (lines 15–16) says `apply_blueprint` stages the expansion as a draft so the per-type schema validates it, so the door reaches the expanded artifact one step after the AI emitted it. ESCALATED to the PM to file: align the blueprint `options` with the door for `select` / `radio`. Not a condition.
4. **objectui `object-metadata-write-guard.derivation.test.ts`** ("the installed server still ACCEPTS a choice with no options") — ANSWERED: not a `main`-red hazard from this landing. The Console Pin Gate is `skipped` on this head because its `console` path filter names `.objectui-sha`, `scripts/build-console.sh`, `packages/spec/package.json`, `tsup.config.ts` and the probe scripts, none touched; when it runs it builds the SPA at the pin, bundling this tree's spec, and runs `check:console-sha` / `check:console-injection` — no objectui tests, and a runtime superRefine cannot break a bundle. `.objectui-sha` reads `31971ff1e28f…` at this head and carries objectui `1563d3e10b` (unlock scan `5947557233`), so the console this repo ships already has the guard the ruling ordered first. The red the dev names arrives in objectui's own CI on its next `@objectstack/spec` bump — the objectui lane's follow-up, as noted.
5. **`canonicalObjectRow` beyond the census** — ANSWERED: right; doc consistency, no behaviour.
6. **`origin/main` merged before the PR; consumer suites at `a9473b8d91`** — ANSWERED: procedural; the head's check-runs are the authority (below), not the dev's local runs.
7. **Full spec suite as a background job; labels; model-free commit trailers** — ANSWERED: procedural and consistent with AGENTS.md.
8. **A4 precision** (a row whose only defect is the missing source counts canonical in the preview; `failed` only when the row also carries an older spelling) — ANSWERED: right, stated in the changeset, pinned.

**New flag, not raised by the dev — ADR-0078's text.** §4 of `docs/adr/0078-no-silently-inert-metadata.md` says "No hard Zod `.refine()` that rejects existing metadata at registration (back-compat)", and its Non-goals list "Hard Zod refinement that rejects existing metadata … not a registration-time crash — existing apps with benign-incomplete instances must keep loading." The door is a hard Zod refinement. It leaves the registration seam that text protects exactly as it was (warn, never throw; a stored row still registers — pinned here), but a code-declared optionless `select` now throws at `ObjectSchema.create()`, which is the BREAKING arm the changeset declares. The maintainer's ruling A positions the door against ADR-0078 explicitly ("one more gate, not a replacement") on a precedent (`0fb8760bec`, the `relationship-without-reference` rule) that shipped the same way without an ADR edit, so the ruling governs here. What is owed is a Tier H landing note on ADR-0078 naming the two completeness rules that are now also parse-door refusals, so the ADR does not read against the schema it governs. ESCALATED for the owning seat to carry to the maintainer. Not a condition on this PR.

**Check-runs on the head at 2026-10-02T10:24Z**: 27 `success`, 2 `skipped` by design (`Console Pin Gate` — path filter; `Packed-tarball smoke` — opt-in), 4 `in_progress`: `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`, `Type Check · workspace`. Green so far includes `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1–3, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Spec property liveness`. An `in_progress` gate is an honest reading, not a pass: the landing still waits for `Test Core` and the `TypeScript Type Check` aggregate to conclude `success`, and this record does not stand in for them.
